prerequisites: Competencies and learning outcomes from preceding courses, especially in mathematics, fluid mechanics, and thermodynamics.
Spanish and English language skills (reading level for English).
Skills in calculator use, graph creation and manipulation, and technical drawing.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft and develop industrial engineering projects concerning the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Industrial Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Ability for occupational risk prevention and protection of workers' and users' health and safety.
Ability to know, select, critically evaluate, and use diverse sources of information.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to problem-solving in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Applied knowledge of thermal engineering.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid mechanical systems and machines.
Understand and apply the fundamentals of fluid machines, systems, and installations.
Perform measurements of fluid mechanical variables and performance tests of fluid machines and systems.
Carry out operation, regulation, and maintenance tasks for fluid systems and installations.
Design, calculate, and project fluid systems and installations.
Handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards related to fluid systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Basic magnitudes and types of fluid machines.
Other installations: pneumatic transport, particle separation, exchangers, etc.
Valves, actuators, and other components of pneumatic and oleo-hydraulic circuits.
Servomechanisms and circuits with proportional valves.
Design and project of oleo-hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

assessment_methods.method: Activities in laboratory practices and group tutorials

assessment_rules: For ordinary and non-early extraordinary calls, the final grade is 80% from the final exam and 20% from practical activities. A minimum of 4 out of 10 points on the exam and a total weighted score of at least 5 out of 10 are required to pass. For the early extraordinary call and all calls for differentiated assessment, the final exam accounts for 90% and a practical activity accounts for 10%. Non-alphanumeric calculators without graphic displays or wireless connections are allowed in the final exam.
